findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote panel ("Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on…"), against the hero's "Write to Mark" button
findings.fault: The pull quote uses the button's shape: the tabula ansata panel with its dovetail handles. The button is that panel filled red; the quote is the same panel outlined, which is how an outlined, second-rank button usually looks. So one look means both "press this" and "this is a quotation", and the quote is a box that looks pressable but does nothing.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page may take the framed quote for a second action and click it, and nothing happens. Once the button is also the house quote frame, the visitor can't learn that the dovetail panel means "get in touch". Angélique will use the quote frame in every post, so the clash will repeat across the site.

findings.where: Site-wide colour role: minium red on the hero name and role line, the article heading, the CINZEL specimen, the motion-sketch words and the nav interpuncts, as well as the "Write to Mark" button
findings.fault: The tile names minium as "headings, the one action", so the primary action's colour isn't kept for the action. The largest red on the first screen is the name and role line, not the button, and every article page will put its headline in the action colour. Red no longer marks the one thing to do.
findings.who_objects: Development-bank staff scanning for how to reach Mark. Red headlines on every article page show no red button, and on the homepage the eye goes to the red name before the button. This weakens the brief's own principle that the one accent "flows to the action".

findings.where: Hero: the "Write to Mark" primary action (mailto:Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com)
findings.fault: The page's one action is a bare mailto link, and the address isn't shown anywhere as text. A visitor whose computer has no mail program set up, or who uses webmail, clicks and gets nothing or the wrong program, and has no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: Staff at multilateral banks and agencies often work on locked-down machines or in webmail. For them, the page's only way to get in touch fails without any message, and the main job of the page fails with it.

findings.where: Motion sketch: the "LAY AGAIN" control, against the article specimen's underlined link "Streamlining the PPP Process…"
findings.fault: "Lay again" is a button that replays the animation where it is, but it's styled as an underlined link, and the underline is the look kept for links that take you somewhere. On this page an underline means both "go somewhere" and "do something here".
findings.who_objects: A visitor, or the layout round copying this tile, can't tell from the look whether an underlined phrase leaves the page or acts in place. The layout round will inherit a link look on buttons.
